html:
SMTO-LLM-0099 — SMTO's automatic retry for this step is used up

GUID: f40fc9b7-3b7c-4b2a-af34-29c404ef9973
Slug: model-generation-recovery-exhausted
Domain: LLM · Subsystem: provider

What happened

  • The model stalled or repeated itself, and SMTO's one automatic retry for this step already ran or was cut short. The task is paused, and work finished so far is saved.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Scroll up in the task to the earlier model message (it didn't start answering, stopped making progress, or kept repeating itself) and follow its steps first. That earlier message names what went wrong; this one only says the automatic retry is used up.
  2. Open Settings › Setup › Model routing, open the Main card, and select Check saved model. This confirms the model service is answering normally before you continue.
  3. Open the paused task and select Resume. Resume gives the step a fresh retry, and actions that already finished are not run again.

What success looks like

  • After Resume, the paused step completes and the task continues without repeating earlier actions.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO or your model service. Restarting SMTO won't give you another automatic retry; only Resume does. Don't change unrelated time limits or budgets.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The decision's single durable generation-quality recovery attempt was already exhausted, or was in flight when the process stopped, so it cannot be dispatched again; completed work is preserved and an explicit Resume starts a new recovery episode.

What this means

  • The decision has already consumed its single generation-quality recovery attempt, or that attempt was in flight when the process stopped. Restart does not reset this durable allowance. The task pauses with accepted operations and their receipts preserved.

Why this can happen

  • A durable recovery record is already in flight or exhausted for this decision episode.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the reported reason and effective settings.

How to fix it

  • Find the preceding error in the task (model_generation_startup_timeout, model_generation_stalled_no_action or model_generation_repetitive) and check provider health for it. Then use Resume, which starts a fresh recovery episode; completed operations keep their receipts and are not replayed. Restarting the Server does not reset this allowance.
  • Inspect the preceding startup, inactivity or repetition error and provider health. Use Resume when ready to start a fresh bounded recovery episode; completed operations retain their receipts.

Retry and execution caution

  • Explicit Resume starts a fresh episode and retains completed tool receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • An explicit Resume starts a new episode and the pending decision completes without replaying earlier operations.

What not to do

  • Do not change an unrelated timeout, budget or policy. Check whether the named setting applies only to a new task.

Technical notes

  • The current decision is rejected before tool authorization when enforcement applies; earlier results are not replayed.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
